page: Microsoft Azure E96-48as_v4 is an EASv4-family virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 14.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 1376 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. The virtualization layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and memory performance, with stress-ng multi-core scoring 64915.93 and PassMark CPU score reaching 51926.65, both placing in the top 25% of tested hardware. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark CPU encryption also rank in the top tier. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with uncached large-block reads at 106.17 GB/sec and writes at 59.74 GB/sec. Large-model LLM text generation represents a performance bottleneck, scoring in the bottom 10% at 2.28 tokens/sec, whereas small-model inference performs strongly.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, this server offers high resource density for memory-bound applications without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The combination of strong multi-core performance and large memory capacity makes it highly suitable for memory-intensive databases, large-scale data decompression, cryptography-heavy applications, and small-model language processing.
